chunks: Ja'far b. 'Ali b. al-Hasan al-Kufi (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan b. 'Ali narrated to me from his grandfather 'Abd Allah b. al-Mughira, from Isma'il b. Muslim al-Sakuni, from al-Sadiq Ja'far b. Muhammad, from his father (peace be upon them both). He said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: The horses of the warriors — their horses will be in Paradise.

key_terms.الجنة: Paradise, the Garden — the eternal abode promised to the righteous
key_terms.الغزاة: warriors, those who go on ghazwa (raid/expedition); participants in jihad in the path of Allah
key_terms.خيول: horses (plural of فرس/خيل) — the primary instrument of cavalry warfare in early Islam

ai.seo_question: Do horses of Islamic warriors go to Paradise according to hadith?
ai.summary: The Prophet Muhammad (SAWA) promises a heavenly reward for the horses used in jihad, declaring that the horses of warriors (ghuzat) will themselves be admitted to Paradise. This prophetic saying was transmitted through Imam al-Sadiq (AS) and his father Imam al-Baqir (AS), reaching the compiler al-Saduq through a Kufan chain. In the early Islamic context, the horse was the most prized and expensive instrument of warfare, and this statement would have been understood as an extraordinary honor — extending divine reward not just to the mujahid but to his animal companion in the cause of Allah.

en.bilal-muhammad: Ja`far b. `Ali b. al-Hasan al-Kufi (ra) narrated to us. He said: My grandfather al-Hasan b. `Ali narrated to me from his grandfather `Abdullah b. al-Mughira from Isma`il b. Muslim al-Sukuni from al-Sadiq Ja`far b. Muhammad from his father (as). He said:
The Messenger of Allah (s) said: The horses of conquerors will be in Paradise.
